The stamp is now written only on a successful admin_request upload (_settle_diagnostics_request ~9151). Only one ask can be in flight, a failed one waits a 300 s retry floor, and the lane-error read-modify-write moved under the same lock, which closes the lost-update between the two writers. Both regression tests fail on HEAD. Nit, not blocking: in _apply_diagnostics_request (~9141), if threading.Thread(...).start() inside _upload_diagnostics_async raises after _diagnostics_request_inflight is set, the outer except logs it but never clears the in-flight marker. Every later ask would then be refused until the tray restarts. Clearing it in that except would close the gap.

_site_refresh_loop (~6383) never raises. It waits on _stop_event (900 s after a success, 120 s after a failure) and saves only a non-None fetch, so an old dashboard or a dead tailnet keeps the cache. feature_enabled reads the cache on every call, and broll_server's origin list has a TTL, so a flipped flag now reaches a running tray. save_site has no other in-process caller, so the fixed .tmp name is not contended. Deferring load-time config keys (smb_unc, SFTP tuning) to the next start is honest: that is config.py's documented contract. Both tests fail on HEAD.

The ALREADY_FIXED claim holds. dashboard db.py mark_file_move_applied (~6278+) has a second arm: `ok and not relink_pending and state in (None,'','done')` updates `relink_pending=0` WHERE applied_at IS NOT NULL AND ok=1 AND relink_pending=1. The companion's second answer from _relink_pending_moves (~8787) is _queue_file_move_answer(id, True, detail): no state and no relink_pending, which is the shape that arm matches. The API validator maps an unknown state to None. Skew: every companion that has RES-10 already sends this shape, so only the dashboard needs deploying. Owned by d-db and uncommitted, so it rests on that group landing.

_on_report_response now takes a re-entrant lock around the fan-out. The only post_once callers are the reporter's own loop and _report_off_cycle's daemon thread. No consumer joins the off-cycle thread, so waiting on the lock cannot deadlock, and re-entrancy covers an inline post on the same thread. The regression test uses a real slow consumer through the real wrapper and fails on HEAD (max concurrency 2).

The filter and the append now run under one hold of _file_move_answers_lock (~8657-8661), and the drain (_file_move_results) takes the same lock for its swap. The property-seam test reproduces the exact interleaving and fails on HEAD. The res-companion-5 test is still green.

app.py:_pid_looks_like_companion (~469-490) decides 'not a companion' from the text `"ccsync" in command.lower()`, so the fix is fail-OPEN for a supported install. installer/macos_bootstrap.sh:152 accepts `--companion-path <path>`. The default ($HOME/.local/ccsync/bin/ccsync-companion) contains 'ccsync', but an owner-chosen path such as /Applications/Sync/companion does not. On that Mac, a live companion's own pid reads as 'not a companion': _pid_holds_the_slot returns False, and _acquire_lock_file lets a second instance start beside the first. That is the outcome the guard exists to prevent: two trays and two sets of rclone lanes, with the 8899 bind failing in one. Suggested fix: also return True when ps names this process's own executable (os.path.basename(sys.executable) when frozen, else sys.argv[0]), which is the same binary the LaunchAgent and self-upgrade relaunch, or match on the realpath of sys.executable. Keep 'ccsync' as a second accepted token. The regression tests only use paths that contain 'ccsync', so they do not cover this. Otherwise the change is fine: win32 is unchanged, ps failure is fail-safe, and not unlinking at shutdown is reasonable.

verdicts.problems: Traced broll_ingest.match_manifest_rows (broll_ingest.py:4096-4182). The two folder-blind tiers run last, keep the _hash_compatible veto and the ord order, so an exact-folder file is never taken by a folder-blind row. The music caller (music_ingest._match_staged) already flattens rel_dir, so this changes nothing there. On HEAD the 4 regression tests fail (checked with a git-archive HEAD copy). One minor residual, not blocking: tier 5 (same_name, :4174) will pair a row and a staged file whose sizes are both known and DIFFERENT. The docstring promises that a provably different file is never paired, but only a hash mismatch is vetoed. For wrong footage to follow, a row's own staged file has to be missing while another staged file of the same name is left unclaimed, which is unlikely, and HEAD's tier 3 has the same gap. A size veto in same_name is safe for b-roll. Before adding one to music, check whether the server rewrites music's size_bytes after the transcode the way it rewrites content_hash.

The real release path exists. ingest_batches.retry_failed (broll/web/app/ingest_batches.py:584) puts proxies_live items back in the queue, and the second /uploaded call with original_uploaded=True reaches _original_landed (broll_ingest.py:3144). _original_landed takes self._lock itself, and its caller does not hold that lock (the lock is not re-entrant), so there is no deadlock. Music can never reach it: music uploads KIND_AUDIO and never KIND_ORIGINAL, so original_uploaded is always False. That means the ITEM_QUEUED base-rig holds are never released by this code. In _note_staging_ended the merge only ever adds names, and removing a name is left to _original_landed. staging_report's new held_bytes key is additive. The new _space_refusal text has no em dash. verdicts.problems: None. jobs_media.py:953 needs both an empty probe codec and ffmpeg's 'does not contain any stream' stderr, so a machine whose ffprobe cannot run still gets a retryable failure. The substring matches ffmpeg 4 and ffmpeg 7 wording. The real-ffmpeg test ran here and was not skipped (22/22 passed), and the retryable guard tests still hold. The result wire is unchanged.

The refusal is too broad, and it is permanent where it used to end in success. job_paths.py safe_stem (_STEM_FORBIDDEN = '/', '\\', ':') raises retryable=False for ':' and '\\'. Those characters are only illegal on Windows. The stem is the multicam name Cards sends (library_engine.py:2445, `self._mp_names.get(mp_uid, mp_uid)`, unsanitised), and Resolve allows ':' in a clip name. The Cards engine itself writes `<name>.ext` on Linux (library_engine.py:3540, 3958). On HEAD, a stem like 'Q&A: Ruskin' failed on Windows companions with a retryable OSError. A Mac companion could write it, and once the retry budget ran out the job was pinned onto the dashboard's Linux engine (cards_exec), which writes the name fine, so the page got its file. Now db.py:10904 turns retryable=False straight into JOB_FAILED: no Mac gets a turn and it is never pinned, so the file the page looks for is never made. The owed cards_exec.py:403 change would make the dashboard refuse it too. Suggested fix: refuse fleet-wide (retryable=False) only for a real separator '/', an empty/'.'/'..' name, a drive-absolute name or a control character. Treat ':' and '\\' as 'not HERE' (retryable=True, or only on os.name == 'nt'), so a Mac or the pinned engine can still write it. The owed cards_exec rule should not copy the Windows-only characters. The rest of the fix (the retryable flag on JobPathError, _placement_retryable, safe_stem wired into jobs_runner._media_paths:1236) is correct.

None blocking. proxy_gen.py:966-972 asks the same _available_fn about ffmpeg_tools.ffprobe_for(ffmpeg_path). That is the path probe_video spawns. `ffprobe -version` exits 0, so ffmpeg_available works for it unchanged, successes are cached for 300 s, and it runs on the generator thread, not a UI thread. The not-done half (the window where ffprobe vanishes inside the success cache) is a fair deferral. The tray wording ('ffmpeg is not installed here') is owed to c-app and is cosmetic.

None. job_paths.resolve refuses a control character up front and wraps any ValueError/OSError from resolve() (ValueError not retryable, OSError retryable). Every job_paths.resolve caller is inside those two handlers (lines 1224, 1232, 1253, 1255). The tests cover media, whisper and a generic ValueError/OSError. It relies on chunk 1's fix, and that fix is on the only path the finding names: sequencer._prune_trash (sequencer.py:1449-1469) reaches the lane only through _maybe_prune_trash, which now takes min_free_bytes=_prune_free_target() (rclone_lane.py ~4543-4582). The fix holds. The connected-device set comes from summarize_connections, which counts CONNECTED devices only. The token 'c:<in+out bytes>' is sent through reporter._lane_liveness for the non-terminal 'syncing' state. Dashboard health.lane_stall reddens it after the 30-minute floor (LANE_STALL_FLOOR_SECONDS=1800). Keep-alive pings from a connected peer keep a slow lane from being called stalled. The state stays syncing, so the sequencer's turn logic is unchanged. Both new tests fail on HEAD copies. One minor overreach, not blocking: at syncthing_lane.py:579, no_peer = bool(connections) and not connections.get('devices'). A 200 answer that simply lacks the 'connections' key still yields a non-empty summary with empty devices (summarize_connections, lines 131-133), so the lane would claim 'not connected'. Only an exception gives {}. This contradicts the builder's 'an unreadable connection list claims nothing' for a malformed-but-successful body. The tray half is correctly owed to c-ui.

Both comparisons now use nfc_key on both sides: _project_rel_for_path (rclone_lane.py ~2396-2402) and _refresh_stray_projects (~3425-3433). Only the comparison is folded: the returned rel is the dashboard's spelling and the reported directory is the disk's. Express still builds its upload rel from the disk path (_express_rel, ~5571), which is the same NFD source the periodic lane A pass already uploads from, so this adds no new name shape. Both tests fail on HEAD. test_rclone_express and test_rclone_lane pass.

transferred += 1 now sits in the non-deletion arm only (rclone_lane.py ~2143-2160). I checked every consumer of result.transferred: _last_run_moved (still transferred+deleted, so the idle backoff is unchanged), the three tray/status detail strings (~3810, 3830, 3866) and express recording (~5889-5895). None depends on deletions being counted as transfers. The express path never deletes. Both tests fail on HEAD. The updated asserts in test_rclone_lane pass.

The Windows output is [[], [{] and [}] with no backslash. I traced this against gobwas/glob's lexer as I recall it (not checked against a live Syncthing): inside a range the lexer reads text up to ']', so '[' and '{' there are literal. Outside a term, ']' and '}' are plain text. The pattern therefore reads correctly whether or not the backslash is an escape. The posix branch is unchanged. On an existing lender, borrowed_folders._ensure_ignores (309-342) sees the new line missing and calls set_ignores with the whole list, so the old backslash lines are replaced, not appended to, and the trailing '**' stays last. Tests fail on HEAD. Minor: the builder calls test_a_plain_name_is_unchanged_on_both_platforms a control, but it also fails on HEAD (TypeError on the new windows= keyword).

The cache records the lowercased editor, write-on-change includes the editor, and a cache is refused only when both names are known and differ. With require_login, sign-out stops the lanes (app.py:6787-6801) and the next sign-in has an identity, so the stated scenario (B signs in, B's first fetch fails) is closed. The halt re-pause reads any_editor=True, which pauses only; the halt release reads without it, which errs toward leaving A's folders paused. project_roots_result (selection.py ~704-718) now also refuses a foreign cache. Those roots are admin-wide, not per person, so this degrades to 'unreachable' instead of using a still-valid mapping. That is harmless but worth knowing. The tests fail on HEAD. The remaining gap is accepted: a pre-upgrade cache with no editor is still read once by a different person.

_repoint (shared_folders.py ~470-496) mirrors the borrowed manager's. It checks _mkdir_allowed, pauses, moves the old directory (which carries .stfolder) through repath._default_move (wired at sequencer.py:343/356), mkdirs, then PATCHes. The unpause now comes from paused_now. A running or just-re-pointed folder with no marker gets marker-missing, which is in PROBLEM_OUTCOMES and so is kept and backed off. It is checked every pass, and reconcile() already returns {} when the root is absent (line 329), so an unplugged drive does not raise it. Not creating the marker is right: an empty marked directory against the old index would read as mass deletion. No other consumer depends on the fixed outcome set. The sentence has no em dash. The tests fail on HEAD, and test_shared_folders (22) passes. Minor: when a re-point is refused (_mkdir_allowed false), 'error' is recorded with no reason, which is generic but true.

The fix does not close the scenario in the finding or the one in its own comment. The finding's failure case is a renamed PC inside SYS-18a's deferred-adoption window. In that window, dashboard api._register_machine (api.py:7341-7445) refuses the adoption but still calls db.upsert_machine for the NEW hostname ('this report is still recorded under its own name below, so both rows exist'). db.machines_of(conn, editor) (db.py:4874) therefore lists the new name. The new _machine_unknown_to (selection.py ~620-633) then returns False, the person-wide fallback does not fire, and untick still returns (True, 'unticked') at selection.py ~575-583 with changed=false. The tray deletes the local copy, and the old hostname's plan brings X back when the rename is adopted. The same applies to the owed d-api 404: the new name is registered, so api_untick would still 200. The fix only covers a hostname that has never reported at all, which is the seconds between a companion starting and its first report. The regression test builds exactly that unrealistic view (machines lacks the hostname), so it does not reproduce the finding. The hunter's second suggestion, 'treat changed=false with the slug absent as nothing to untick here rather than success before a local delete', is what the real case needs, and it is not implemented. As written, untick() still reports success for a no-op removal. Secondary: the widening also fires for a computer an admin has just forgotten (CR-76) and that has not yet re-reported. It removes the tick from every one of the person's computers. That is under-sharing, the 'safe' direction, but it is a bigger blast radius than the no-op it replaces.

verdicts.problems: PARTIAL is an honest label and the fix is right. I ran the new tests on a HEAD copy: all 4 picker tests error there because the names they use do not exist in HEAD. On the working tree they pass. I also probed the real _tk_pick on this Windows box (scratch script, 1.5 s timeout, both kinds). WM_CLOSE to the #32770 dialog closed it about 0.35 s after the timeout, pick_media_sources returned [] in 1.85 s, _live_picker was cleared, the lock was released, no picker thread was left, and the interpreter was freed on its own thread. Joining the open picker and reading the answer as the opened dialog's kind both behave correctly: a folder answer goes to the folder walk and a files answer goes to the files branch. Every other caller of _popup_active_lock in app.py uses acquire(blocking=False), so taking the lock on the request thread and releasing it on the picker thread (a plain threading.Lock) cannot deadlock anything. PICKER_BUSY_MESSAGE contains no em dash. Both owed items are correct and necessary. Without them the lock half does nothing: nothing registers a lock, and PickerBusy is caught by broll_server.py:2003's generic except, which shows the old message. The owed app.py line is now ~1613, not ~1500, but the anchor text identifies it. Minor, non-blocking: (a) popup.py pick_media_sources/_start_picker: if Thread.start() raises after lock.acquire, the popup lock and a never-done _live_picker leak for the life of the process. The window is tiny. (b) Once c-app registers the lock, an abandoned macOS panel, which cannot be closed from another thread, holds _popup_active_lock indefinitely, so apply_upgrade stands down for as long as it is up. HEAD already parked the main-thread dispatcher in that case, so this is about as bad as before, not a new class of failure. (c) A waiter that times out closes a dialog that a later joiner is still waiting on. That is an edge case. (d) The log says 'within 2s' for a 1.5 s timeout (%.0f), which is cosmetic.

settings_window.py:214-222 tags the blocked summary as INFO only when blocked.reason is in tray._BLOCKED_INFORMATIONAL (frozenset {'no_selection'}, tray.py:170), the same set and the same key that tray._blocked_line reads. Other reasons keep BLOCKING, and the guard test covers that. _help_first moves HELP only for style=='warning', and INFO maps to muted, so HELP no longer jumps for an empty plan. The regression test fails on HEAD and passes now. No other surface is touched.

tray_native.py:1810-1835: while the menu is open, _apply_menu_now defers and sets _menu_rebuild_pending. menuDidClose_ then goes through _menu_did_close, which clears the flag and queues the pending rebuild with _darwin_after_current (addOperationWithBlock_ even when already on main). The open menu's watcher and targets therefore stay referenced, and a menu action is dispatched from the tracking stack before the queued rebuild runs. The flag is shared with tray.py's guard (menu_open_flag), and only the watcher's menuWillOpen_ sets it (grep: tray_native.py:1565), so it cannot be set spuriously and hold a rebuild forever. The regression tests fail on HEAD and pass now. They fake AppKit, so none of this has run on a Mac, which the builder states.

close() now records _close_requested and sets _closed itself only when no window thread is alive. Otherwise _serve's finally sets it (popup.py:2220-2223), so wait_closed means the window is gone. _build_and_show checks the flag after the build and before run_dialog, and destroys the root and returns inside the try, so its finally still runs cleanup on the building thread. _tick honours the flag in case the after() could not be marshalled (_tkinter's roughly 1 s pre-mainloop wait, then a raise that is caught). Removing the old _open.clear() in the except path is correct: _open now clears only when the thread exits, so open() cannot start a second thread over a live one. The regression tests fail on HEAD and pass now. Negligible residual: a close() between open()'s Thread() assignment and start() still sets _closed early, but the build then sees the flag and destroys the root on its own thread, so no window is shown and no cross-thread free happens.

The deferral is honest. The hunter's option (a) holds _popup_active_lock for as long as the monitor window is up. That can be hours of a b-roll batch, during which every fixer popup, licence or update dialog is refused and apply_upgrade stands down. That is a product trade-off, not an obvious fix. Option (b) only corrects comments in app.py, which belongs to c-app. The decision is correctly handed to the owner or lead.

tray.py: sign-in, typed-confirmation and credentials now wrap everything after tk.Tk() in except BaseException, which calls _discard_half_built and then re-raises. Update and scripting-warning initialise root=None and discard in their existing except, and keep return False. The earlier failure path in each builder (tk.Tk() itself failing) is unchanged. release_root (ui_dispatch.py:1035) never raises and destroys on the building thread, and the helper runs on that same thread. The traceback's frame locals may keep the interpreter pinned, but the window is destroyed, which is the point, and pinning is ui_dispatch's documented safe fallback. The diff is otherwise a pure re-indent: the 474-line diff contains no logic changes beyond these. The regression tests fail on HEAD, 5 of 5, and pass now.

tray_native.py: _icon_handle's lookup and insert, and _teardown's snapshot and clear, now run under _hicon_lock, and DestroyIcon is called outside the lock, so the iteration can no longer be mutated. run()'s finally puts _stopped.set() in a nested finally, so stop() never waits 5 s on a raising teardown. A late icon assignment after teardown can leak one HICON at process exit, which does not matter. Both regression tests fail on HEAD and pass now. I reran 671 tests across the touched suites (new file, test_popup, test_settings_window, test_tray, test_tray_native_main_thread, test_tk_interpreter_hygiene, test_broll_server): all passed.

The focus-ring half was waved away as NOT_A_DEFECT on a measurement I cannot reproduce. My real-Tk probe on this Windows machine used the companion venv, gave the window the foreground and cleared UISF_HIDEFOCUS with WM_CHANGEUISTATE. theme.neon_button (bd=0, relief=flat, highlightthickness=0, theme.py:465-468) showed 0 changed pixels between its focused and unfocused states. A flat Button with highlightthickness=0 and bd=1 also showed 0. The same flat Button with highlightthickness=1 or 2 showed 66-70 changed pixels, and a default tk.Button showed 66. So on Windows, highlightthickness=0 DOES remove the only focus cue. The new neon_button docstring (theme.py:449-453, 'highlightthickness=0 does NOT hide keyboard focus on Windows ... the focus cue is the dotted box') is factually wrong. The hunter's failure scenario still stands: 'a keyboard-only user cannot tell which button Space will press'. It is sharpened by this fix, because confirm_dialog now puts focus on CANCEL (popup.py about line 2543) with no visible cue. The fix is still owed: give neon_button highlightthickness>=1 with highlightbackground=BG and a visible highlightcolor, or draw focus some other way, such as a <FocusIn>/<FocusOut> fg swap. The other parts are sound: MUTED #8a8a96 (>=5.28:1 on BG, FIELD and PANEL), the 'dest:' label moved to MUTED, Escape cancels confirm with Return left unbound, and notice binds Return and Escape and focuses OK. verdicts.problems: Traced the path. When the staging rename fails, staged == src and the conversion runs in place. On a stop, the new branch (companion/src/ccsync_companion/ytdl_executor.py:2639-2652) moves src onto staged_source_name, which is sweepable. _download_one:2489 then sees _should_stop and calls _cleanup_current -> clear_partials, which removes it. The probe-stop branch (:2566-2580) already had the same shape, and the staged branch was covered by 4462a2a. If the retry rename fails too, the code only logs a warning. That is an honest fallback, since it is the same scanner lock that forced the in-place path. The regression test fails on HEAD (confirmed in a scratch copy with HEAD's four modules) and passes now. It drives the real _ensure_edit_ready and only makes os.replace refuse the first staging rename. No wire change, no em dash.

heartbeat() (ytdl_executor.py:1218-1226) now raises CredentialLost on 401/403/404. 2xx and 5xx behave as before. _call still raises LeaseLost on 410 before this point, and the only caller is _heartbeat_loop:2139, which catches CredentialLost before LeaseLost and then does hand_back plus lose_lease (lose_lease kills the process tree). broll_ingest's LeaseLost is unrelated. Server side: routes_fleet.heartbeat -> require_fleet_caller (403) -> _job_or_404 (404) -> 410. A 404 only happens when the job row is gone, and the route has existed since launch, so there is no skew risk against 0.7.57 or older. One small inaccuracy: on a 404 (job deleted) the hand-back sentence at :2141-2144 says 'The server is downloading the rest of these clips', which is not true for a deleted job. This is cosmetic. clip_status/manifest 403s are not treated as verdicts, but the heartbeat catches the case within one 30 s interval, which the finding accepts as a minimum. The tests fail on HEAD and pass now.

The backoff at ytdlp_manager.py:1236 and :1277 fires only when action == ACTION_FAILED. Two other enabled passes publish ok=False and still wait the full 86400 s, even though capabilities() (ytdl_executor.py:971) refuses every job while ok is False. That is the finding's shape exactly. (1) ytdlp_manager.py:1141-1146: an install that succeeds but whose version() then comes back None ('installed yt-dlp (version unreadable)') publishes ok=False with ACTION_INSTALLED. A fresh binary being AV-scanned during a cold PyInstaller --version is the case VERSION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS exists for, and the next pass would read it and go ok=True. (2) :1157-1160: ACTION_UPDATED with ok=False (the update ran but the version is unreadable or still below the floor). Both leave local downloads off for 24 h with no retry. The fix should also count `enabled and not status.get('ok')` as a failed pass (excluding the ACTION_CHECKED override branch if wanted), and the test should cover the installed-but-unreadable pass. The ACTION_FAILED part itself is correct: the tests fail on HEAD, the backoff 300*2^(n-1) is capped at the daily or 900 s cadence and resets on success.

swap_in's last rung now returns (None, reason) (ytdl_executor.py:1735-1745). There is exactly one caller, _ensure_edit_ready. verdicts.problems: The fix is mostly right. PARTIAL is honest, since the DSM half is owed to d-ops. Against the HEAD api.py copy, 3/3 regression tests fail. But the merge still erases some existing keys, which is the same defect in a narrower form. dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/api.py:4697 keeps an existing sshpubkey line only if _key_identity() recognises it. _key_identity uses looks_like_ssh_pubkey, and nas/base.py:24 SSH_KEY_PREFIXES lists only ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ssh-dss and ecdsa-sha2-nistp*. So a hardware-key line (sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com, sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com), a certificate line (ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com) or any other unlisted type on the account is silently dropped on approve. I probed it: an existing sk-ssh-ed25519 line, a cert line and one ssh-ed25519 line were merged with a new key, and the write was 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAone pc1\nssh-ed25519 AAAAtwo pc2'. The docstring's claim that existing keys are kept is false for those lines. Fix: keep every non-blank line that is not a '#' comment verbatim, and use _key_identity only for the duplicate check. Normal case is fine: the TrueNAS PUT of the merged text goes through the same create_or_update_editor refusals, and DSM's '(installed)' marker yields no lines and logs.

The target is now Proxy/<dest.stem><suffix>. The self-target skip, the staging path for case-folding filesystems (TrueNAS SMB datasets are often case-insensitive) and the collision refusal are correct. There is one call site (api.py:2960), and undo goes through the same function symmetrically. 4/4 regression tests fail on HEAD, and test_file_moves.py is green. The companion half is honestly owed to c-sync: file_moves.move_proxy_siblings still uses candidate.name. Minor note, not blocking: api.py:2843 also respells the proxy on a PLAIN move whenever the proxy's stem differs from the original's only by case or NFC/NFD. The companion keeps candidate.name locally, so until the owed change lands that edge costs one lane B re-download plus a trash per holding machine. Using dest.stem only when _proxy_stem_key(dest.stem) != _proxy_stem_key(src.stem), or when their spellings differ, would keep plain moves byte-identical to HEAD.

The before-validators on LaneReportIn, TransferIn, CompletedIn and MediaClipIn reuse _bound_to_field_caps (api.py:7481). That helper truncates str and list and clamps ge/le, and these models have no ge/le numerics. name min_length=1 still rejects. ReportIn-level lists (lanes <=32, completed <=256) still raise, but the companion already sends completed[:200] and 3 lanes, so there is no open path. The edited tests pinned the defect and were correctly moved to 200. The new tests fail on HEAD (422). 84 tests pass across hardening, report_endpoint and the new file. The companion-side cap for older dashboards is honestly owed to c-core. A clip file_path over 1024 characters is now stored truncated rather than 422ing the report, which is the right trade.

_refuse_archived_project runs in create_tree_project before mkdir and marker, in adopt_folder before writing a marker on an unmarked folder, and in _register_project, which catches the marked-folder adopt and is the only tail for both. The two ui.py callers (ui.py:1273, 1334) and the two JSON routes all pass through it. The message has no em dash. The 3 tests answer 200 on HEAD, and test_project_setup.py is green.

revoke_user(username, by, except_sid) exists with that signature in sessions.py:293. It runs after commit, is never-raise, and the admin's own sid is kept via the cached request.state.ccsync_session. The sync route runs in the threadpool. The test fails on HEAD. PARTIAL is honest, since the Users-page [ SET ] (ui.py partial_admin_set_password ~:2876) is owed to d-ui. The builder extended the fix to the NAS branch of api_admin_set_password, which the local-only finding did not require. For consistency, note that the same NAS-mode reset door also exists in the create-or-update routes when a password is supplied for an EXISTING account: api.py:4356-4358 and ui.py:2750 (_create_or_update_editor_sync). Neither revokes sessions, and neither is in the owed list. That is out of the finding's local-mode scope, so it is a note, not a failure.

VerifyIn.arch is optional and truncated, and a non-string becomes None, so a sign-in never 422s on it. api_verify passes a withheld sink and sets upgrade_none_reason only when there is no offer. It uses the report reply's shape and the same _upgrade_info. Skew is fine both ways: 0.9.77 ignores the new key and sends no arch, and an older dashboard ignores arch. The tests fail on HEAD. PARTIAL is honest: the companion identity.py arch/reason work and the app.py sign_in change are what actually stop a sign-in clearing a standing refusal, and both are owed. The machine-targeted offer genuinely cannot be served at /verify.

verdicts.problems: Traced cards.py:420-463. CardsGate now matches BLOCKED_PATHS and AGENT_PREFIX against three readings of each sub-path: raw, with runs of '/' collapsed, and normpath-resolved. The forwarded scope is unchanged. The flat `/cards//p/...` form goes to `_not_here` in CardsDispatch (cards.py:529), so it cannot reach the gate unguarded. The extra readings can only block more, and I found no legitimate page path that normalises onto a blocked one. The regression tests fail on HEAD: I built a scratch mirror from `git show HEAD` and got a real 200 `{'ok': True, 'path': '/api/root'}` and a missing `_gate_readings`. All pass on the tree.

Both halves close the path. (1) `cards_agent_result` goes first to `pool.handed_engine(editor, id)`, which `cards_agent_pending` records only after an edit with an id is handed out (cards_tunnel.py:484-494, 510-519). `drop()` and `stop_all()` clear `_handed`. `open()` replaces only a FAILED entry, and a failed entry never handed anything out. (2) `note_visit` no longer flips `_where` on every poll. Only a navigation, or a page going quiet for 120 s, moves it (cards_pool.py:450-474). The dispatcher computes `entering` with the same test `on_enter` used (cards.py:554). I checked the other repo (agent.py:1150-1224): `agent_pending`/`agent_result` key on `_req['id']`, which matches what is recorded. Residue, noted but not blocking: `_handed` is keyed per editor, not per (editor, machine), so one editor running two Cards agents still hits the old refusal. The builder names this as logic-cards-3. Also, with a phone left awake in B, `_where` stays on B while the user edits in an already-open laptop tab in A until that tab is reloaded. That is deterministic where HEAD flapped, and it matches the 'last episode opened' rule. Tests fail on HEAD (mirror: 'that request is no longer open'; note_visit had no `enter` kwarg).

broll.py:220-247 and music.py:230-257. On every gated path `login_gate` calls `auth.get_session_user` before `call_next` (app.py:1323), which fills `scope['state']['ccsync_session']`. The gate therefore takes the resolution that already accounts for previous secrets and revocation. The fallback is the cookie read with previous secrets, used only on login_gate's bypassed paths or with no dashboard in front. Its minor residue predates this change: the fallback does not consult the session store and takes the first cookie. ytdl.py (d-ops) chose to call `auth.get_session_user(Request(scope))` instead. That is the more uniform rule, but the practical exposure on broll/music's bypassed paths (share, ingest with token, fleet) is negligible. The PARTIAL status and the owed YtdlGate item are honest: the d-ops diff to ytdl.py already carries the equivalent fix. Tests fail on HEAD.

`fleet_facts` now carries `reported_at`. That column is the SERVER clock: the db.py upsert docstring says `now` 'lands in both reported_at... and received_at'. `policy_refusal` refuses a machine silent for more than 15 min, and it sits second, after the fleet halt (jobs.py:846-854). `machine_facts` (the offer and claim path) carries no `reported_at`, so a reporting machine is never self-refused. `offers_for_machine` replaces the caller's own row in the lazy fleet read (jobs.py:1024-1025). A companion keeps reporting every 60 s while it works (reporter.py:508; the jobs backoff stops asking for work, not reporting). REASON_SILENT is non-transient and ordered after every code a live machine can clear. The Cards client reads `schedulable` only (fleet_jobs.py:209), and alerts `_check_jobs_starved` ignores unmapped codes, so there is no regression there. One semantic shift worth knowing: a TARGETED job whose target is switched off now answers `machines_not_reporting` (non-transient) instead of `target_away`. That matches section 10's own wording ('not transient -- ... until that machine is switched on'). Minor: a site with `dashboard_report_interval` above 15 min would read as silent. Tests fail on HEAD.

cards_pool.py:586-595: a non-admin may close an episode only when it has no occupants or they are the only one. The admin path and the FAILED-entry path are unchanged. cards_landing.py:130-139 builds the confirm from `last_in_other_than(me)`, and `seen` keys and `me` are both lowercased. Minor stale copy, not blocking: the cap refusal (cards_pool.py:562-565) still says 'Ask whoever is in one to press [ CLOSE ]'. In a two-person episode neither person can now close it, so that advice is only true for a sole occupant. Tests fail on HEAD.

The seat stamp moved out of `local_engine`, which every agent call goes through, into `_seat()`. `_seat()` is called only for a full state push, a playhead ping whose (playhead, ph_uid) differs from the engine's, or a result (cards_tunnel.py:417-422, 522). I checked the other repo: the pool engine sets `self.playhead` and `self.ph_uid` in `agent_state` and `publish` (agent.py:351-352, library_engine.py:4641-4642). `push_loop` (agent.py:2025-2075) re-sends the unchanged playhead as its AGENT_PING_S heartbeat, so the comparison reads the heartbeat as idle as intended. `_playhead_moved` is evaluated before `_local` mutates the engine. security-1's liveness intent still holds: Resolve-side edits move the version, which triggers a full push, and a moving playhead pings. `note_agent(editor, engine)` stamps the engine actually used, so a result routed to its handing engine seats the right episode. Test fails on HEAD.

The downgrade to low is honest: `can_pin` requires `available()` at pin time, and any later engine drains the job. `_NO_ENGINE` is set in `tick()` when `not self.available()` and cleared on the next available pass and in `stop()`. The pinned summary appends a waiting sentence, with no em dash. One small inaccuracy: `available()` (cards_exec.py:205-210) is also false when an engine IS open but its checkout lacks `fleet_execute`. After a Cards redeploy that drops the seam, the summary would claim 'no Timeline Cards episode is open... runs as soon as somebody opens one', which is untrue. Setting `_NO_ENGINE` only when `self.engine is None` would be exact. That redeploy is an edge case and not worth blocking. Test fails on HEAD.

cards_ai.py:1183-1206: `_trimmed` keeps every leading pair whose user message has the corpus shape (`_is_corpus_message`: a list content whose first block is text, which no ordinary turn has), then the last max(1, MAX_TURNS - lead) pairs. User/assistant order is preserved and at least one recent turn is always kept. A conversation whose first message is not a corpus keeps `lead=1`, which is HEAD's behaviour. The existing 40-turn test is unchanged and green. The new test fails on HEAD (parts 1-3 were cut). verdicts.problems: No problems found in the ytdl half. The fix is at ytdl.py:186-212. In production the scope carries the dashboard app, so YtdlGate._session_user asks auth.get_session_user(Request(scope)). That returns login_gate's cached verdict from auth.py:662, which already accepts DASH_SESSION_SECRET_PREVIOUS. When no app is in the scope, the fallback passes previous=previous_session_secrets(self._settings), and a None settings gives (). I ran both regression tests against HEAD's ytdl.py in a scratch tree: they fail there ({'user': None} vs 'bob') and pass on the working tree. The broll.py/music.py halves are honestly marked OWED to d-cards, and both files already carry an uncommitted diff. This is dashboard-only with no wire change, so version skew does not apply. Minor, not blocking: on routes login_gate lets through before reading the session (for example /ytdl/api/config/ytdl-client), a browser cookie now costs one sessions-table read on the event loop. Companions send no cookie, so this is negligible.

The new pattern at crash_report.py:73-78 redacts all 8 env-style and quoted cases; all 8 fail on HEAD (confirmed in a scratch copy). The 'already redacted' guard tests still pass. The replacement keeps the prefix, for example DASH_SESSION_SECRET=<redacted>. There is no nested quantifier, so no catastrophic backtracking. A side effect to note: traceback source lines such as `self._secret = ...` or `api_key = ...` are now partly redacted too. The comment names over-redaction as the cheap direction, and it can only hide, never leak. The companion copy is OWED to c-ui, and that is recorded.

record_offer_state (release_feed.py:916-990) now selects through select_offered_records, the same rule _apply_policy uses. It keeps versions at or below the chosen one for SYS-2's behind-count and raises feed_publish_refused only for the selected record. check_now fills cache['channel'] (line 849) before its call at line 897. offered_dashboard_version (line 698) gives package_store.what_is_running the pointed dashboard. The new channel argument is optional, and None means the old highest-wins rule. The six regression tests fail on HEAD, by assertion or a missing API; the what_is_running test fails with '99.0.0' != '0.7.57'. test_sweep_2026_09_04_dashboard, test_invariants and test_packages all pass. Behaviour change worth knowing: a pointer that names a version the feed does not carry now makes that platform offer nothing, where before it offered everything. That matches _apply_policy and is intended.

_dashboard_auto_apply_reason (release_feed.py:1160-1177) filters code_updates and runtime_updates to the pointed version when the channel has a dashboard pointer. With no pointer the old rule stays. The regression test fails on HEAD ('9.9.9' applied instead of the pointed '9.9.8'). The note contains no em dash. Deferring auto-rollback when a pointer moves back is honest: it would be an unattended downgrade across a forward-only schema, and the hunter only noted it in passing. Cosmetic: when the pointer names a version the feed does not carry, the note says '(none named)', which is slightly inaccurate.

On the production path, the gate now uses login_gate's cached (username, sid, tracked) verdict. That gives it the same last-wins cookie and the session-store revocation check. The broll/music copies are OWED to d-cards, as for bug-dash-ops-2.

_finish_install (cli_tools.py:1243-1270) carries forward every replaced version that is still on disk and inside its grace. It removes duplicates of `previous` and the reinstalled version, and _prune_old_versions spares all of them. sweep_superseded retires each version on its own clock and rewrites the record through _set_superseded. The newest entry stays in previous_version/superseded_at_epoch, so the older-dashboard skew case holds. The only callers of _prune_old_versions and sweep_superseded are in cli_tools, and sweep's return value is ignored at line 1552. The change to test_cli_auto_update.py is justified, because the old test pinned the defect. The regression tests fail on HEAD (2.1.100 pruned). The cli suites pass.

write_report (crash_report.py:146-164) now uses O_EXCL with -1..-99 suffixes and keeps mode 0o600. verdicts.problems: Traced it end to end. music/web/musicweb/db.py:581-627 claim_dest asks the same three questions allocate_name asks (disk in both spellings, tracks, and the ledger's unlanded dest_name with the same exclusion list as reserved_names), then creates an O_EXCL placeholder under NAME_LOCK. ingest_batches.write_item_result:949-1044 holds NAME_LOCK from allocate_name through the commit, so neither side can pick a name inside the other's gap. There is no lock-order deadlock: claim_dest takes no sqlite write lock, and index_music.upsert commits every item. The fallback move works over the placeholder on Linux (rename) and on Windows (rename fails, copy2 then overwrites it). Every unique_dest caller in non-test code has been switched: routes_ingest.py:382 and music_index/ingest.py:145. Tests: new file passes; against a git archive of HEAD the 3 named tests fail; full music/web suite 640 passed; indexer 50 passed. Two nits, neither blocking. (1) At db.py:571 a locked-db OperationalError in the ledger query is read as 'no promises', which fails open. (2) NAME_LOCK is per process, so a base-rig inline ingest in another process is covered only by the O_EXCL file plus the DB check. The owed rclone --ignore-existing is an honest defence-in-depth item for another group.

Confirmed on HEAD: release(cancelled) left indexed/uploading tracks rows in place, and nothing else ever deletes them. The fix, ingest_batches.py:1265-1325, runs inside release's transaction. It is conservative: when share_root_ready says no, when the stat is unsure, or when the file is present, the row is kept. FKs are on through db.con, and schema.sql cascades windows/tags/axes/peaks and SETs NULL on ingest_items.track_id/duplicate_of. drop_proxy runs after the commit and scores_stale is set. It covers all three entry points: the fleet release route (which settles scores), the browser cancel route and expire_stale_leases (these two leave the marker for the next settle). On skew: companion 0.9.77 calls release('cancelled') only from an explicit cancel, and it stops its upload queue first (broll_ingest.cancel:1387-1398), so no in-flight upload is expected after the rows go. Residual edge, not blocking: combined with bug-music-ytdl-3's sample change, a brand-new library on an empty (unmounted) mountpoint now reads as ready, so a cancel there drops rows whose audio may have landed on the real NAS. mark_uploaded could never have succeeded in that state either. The regression test fails on HEAD; the guards pass.

This is the same defect and the same fix as bug-music-ytdl-4 (ingest_batches.release / _drop_unlanded_tracks, ingest_batches.py:1265-1325), and I verified it there. test_cancelling_drops_the_rows_whose_audio_never_landed fails on HEAD and passes now.

The fix leaves out only ledger states 'indexed'/'uploading' (config.py:571-572, _UNLANDED). A 'failed' item also keeps its track_id and its tracks row: retry_failed's docstring at ingest_batches.py:571-573 says 'track_id and dest_name STAY', and an upload that failed never landed. So the same shape is still open. Example: a first drop into a new library where item 1's upload fails. Every later result, and every item of the next batch, hits allocate_name -> share_root_ready. The sample is then only that failed row with no file, so the answer is 503 'is there but empty ... not mounted', until someone presses retry. The fix should also leave out failed items that hold a track_id, or at least those whose file is absent. Separately (minor): library_has_tracks now answers false when the only rows are unlanded, which lets _create_share_root_on_first_run (routes_ingest.py:319) mkdir a missing mount root in more cases than HEAD did (the music-1 hazard). Tests: the two named tests fail on HEAD and pass now, and test_share_gate passes.

style.css:714-737 replaces the 150px height with a grid-template-rows 0fr->1fr animation on the pane. The pane has exactly one child (.paneinner, app.js:206-235), so the single-row grid is valid. The closed state zeroes the vertical padding and bottom border, and closePane removes the element after 280 ms anyway. The canvas keeps its fixed 64px CSS height, and the width comes from the grid column, so the waveform draw is unaffected. The regression test fails on HEAD (height:150px) and passes now. test_theme_css passes in the full suite (640 passed). Browser support: grid-template-rows transitions need Chrome 107+ / Safari 16+, and older browsers snap open without animating.

The rail filters, include-unknown and [ include them ] now correctly re-run the search (app.js:599-602 refreshResults, handlers at 636/712/925/943). The sort control is the problem. sort.onchange (app.js:919) now calls runSearch, but runSearch sends filterFields() only (app.js:518-532). The sort param exists only in filterParams (537), and /api/search ranks by match (routes_api.py:249/269). So during a search, changing the sort pays for a fresh CLAP embed and gives back the same order. The control silently does nothing. HEAD at least visibly sorted, though it did so by dropping the search. The hunter's suggested fix (ui-music-ytdl-web.md) said to hide the sort control, or say it does not apply, while a search is showing, and that half was not done. The ledger line 'Changing the sort during a search re-runs the search' is accurate, but the editor-facing defect (a control that looks live and does nothing) remains. Tests fail on HEAD and pass now.

The editor's own STOP is phase 'cancelled', so announceHandBack (app.js:2749-2760) correctly stays quiet for it. watchHandBack (2765-2785) polls with a 1 s budget, stops on a 404 (a companion older than /ytdl/progress, so no skew problem), on finished/cancelled, or at 240 s. miForgetRunDrop clears a drop that was not the batch's. music/web/static/ingest.js:680 calls it whenever `mi.running` was true when the batch turns terminal, and `mi.running` is not specific to this page's own run. (1) The list-poll re-attach after a reload sets `mi.running = true` (ingest.js:1206-1207), and so does miTakeOver (1406-1407). The claim 'a batch that the list poll re-attached after a reload does not clear a new drop' is therefore false, and the guard test test_a_reattached_batch_does_not_clear_a_new_drop (music/web/tests/test_bug_hunt_2026_09_24_w2_music-ytdl.py:699-703) passes only because it drives running=false, which the real re-attach path never produces. (2) Drops are accepted during a run: miHandleDrop, the picker and miAddItems (ingest.js:237-266, 327-347, 480-497) have no running guard, and only prepare/precheck return early. So an editor who drops new tracks while their batch, a re-attached batch or a taken-over batch is running loses those new, unstaged tracks without any notice when that batch ends, because mi.items is emptied wholesale. Fix: record which items went into the batch when this page ran it (local_ids or the stagingId in miRun, e.g. `mi.ranItems`/`mi.ranStagingId`), remove only those, and leave re-attached and taken-over batches alone. The guard test should drive the real re-attach state (running=true, an item added after the run). The 'Last batch' heading change in miRenderLive (~1088-1093) is fine.

The core fix is sound. A double click verifies once, a stale result is dropped and does not jump to show_install, the worker catches its own exceptions so the busy flag cannot stay set, and the url is read on the Tk thread. TestOneRequestAtATime fails on HEAD for behavioural reasons (measured). The fix does add a stuck-looking state. If the editor presses BACK while a verification is in flight and comes back to STEP 3 (a new page), VERIFY on the new page is not greyed out, and clicking it or pressing Enter hits the guard at onboard.py:942: it prints 'still verifying the last attempt...' and returns. When the old result lands, onboard.py:992 drops it because the page differs. It clears _verify_in_flight but never updates the current page, so the new page reads 'still verifying the last attempt...' forever, and nothing tells the editor to press VERIFY again. Suggested fix: when a dropped result finds the editor back on a sign-in page, clear or replace that page's signin_status_lbl; or key the guard on the page and let a new page start its own request. CHECK CONNECTION has the same shape (onboard.py:828): a click on a revisited Tailscale page is ignored silently until the previous check returns. That is bounded at about 25 s by the tailscale/probe timeouts, but it gives no feedback.

verdicts.problems: Traced it. retract_record (publish_feed.py:782-800) is the only place that pops `current`, and the new guard (publish_feed.py main(), after the 'nothing to do' check) runs before the dry-run print, write_channel and github_upload, so a refused run signs and uploads nothing. The only local side effect is the artifact copy into feed/, which already happens today. The guard lets through a retract of a non-current build, a retract of the only build, and a same-run --set-current or --artifact --make-current. A --set-current that names the version being retracted is refused through retracted_keys. The recall line publish_latest prints (recall_argv) fills in --set-current <previous> or --allow-no-current, so it passes the guard. The docs match the code. No wire change. The touched suites pass: 190 passed (w2 file, test_publish_feed, test_publish_latest, test_release_scripts).

The main fix is right: same bytes moves the pointer, different bytes prints the --set-current line, and it never moves the pointer backwards. meta['sha256'] is always there because verify() checks it. One gap remains. move_pointer (tools/publish_latest.py, the new function near line 210) builds its own argv and never forwards `extra`, so the --allow-key-rotation that main() adds to `extra` (publish_latest.py:416-417) is dropped. The new REL-7 check on --set-current (publish_feed.py, the `before_keys`/`signing_id` block) then refuses a staged record signed with a rotated key and tells the operator to pass --allow-key-rotation. Passing it to publish_latest changes nothing, so the operator is stuck in a loop and can only get out by running publish_feed by hand. Fix: move_pointer should append --allow-key-rotation when args.allow_key_rotation is set, and a test should pin that. Smaller point: --min-version and --notes are silently ignored on the pointer-only path. They should at least be named in the output.

Skipping the probes when the journal is at publish or later is right. The new onboard.exe reuse (tools/ship.ps1, the `$rebuildOnboard` block before `$pkgArgs`) is under-guarded. (1) The journal is written with step 'publish' BEFORE pkgRc is checked (ship.ps1, `Save-ShipStep -Step "publish"` right after `& powershell @pkgArgs`), so a step 2b that failed with exit 1 still counts as ResumedPastPublish, even when it published nothing. (2) Neither the probe skip nor the reuse checks the journal's `installer_version` against the current $InstallerVersion. -Resume only compares the companion version (ship.ps1 ~line 409). So take the case build_editor_package.ps1:1292 tells the operator to handle: the installer upload 409s, the operator bumps $InstallerVersion (windows_bootstrap.ps1 + steps.py), then runs ship.cmd -Resume. The installer collision probe is skipped for the NEW version. The old onboard.exe is newer than the companion exe, so it is reused without a rebuild. build_editor_package then publishes that exe under the new version, taken from windows_bootstrap.ps1, while the exe still carries the old steps.py INSTALLER_VERSION. Its staleness check (build_editor_package.ps1:823-844) only warns. HEAD always rebuilt, so this is a new way to ship a stale installer. Fix: gate both the probe skip and the reuse on `"$($prior.installer_version)" -eq $InstallerVersion`, and require onboard.exe to be newer than onboarding\*.py and installer\windows_bootstrap.ps1 as well as the companion exe (the same inputs build_editor_package's staleness check uses). Test note: test_a_resumed_publish_reuses_the_onboard_exe_it_published only checks the source text, so it would not catch this.

recall_argv builds the argv from FEED_REPO and FEED_DIR.name ('feed', relative to the repo root, which is also where the printed `python tools\publish_feed.py` has to be run from). It uses the --retract KIND/PLATFORM/VERSION form that argparse accepts, and it carries --set-current <previous> or --allow-no-current, so it passes the new logic-release-2 guard. The test parses the printed line with publish_feed.parse_args and runs it against a local feed. It prints one line per record. On the previous-current key check: the previous record is normally signed by a key the retracted build bakes, so the rollback is not refused by REL-7 in the normal case.

kind_extras_signed() matches sign_release.py:379-380. publish_feed calls sign_release in-process and passes no --emit-kind-extras, and the env var reaches it through the subprocess environment. With extras off the gate is now a NOTE; with CCSYNC_EMIT_KIND_EXTRAS=1 the SYS-7 refusal is unchanged. This is the fix the hunter and verifier med-12 asked for; the verifier judged the customer side's missing check to be the deliberate REL-4/REL-16 policy. stderr is now echoed on success in both publish() and move_pointer(). The side effect is noise only: every sign_release NOTE now shows up. One thing to note, not a defect: with extras off, the operator no longer has to publish the dashboard bundle first. That refusal was the only thing enforcing the order, even though customers never checked it; the NOTE says so explicitly.

--set-current is a real pointer-only move. It refuses a record the channel does not carry, a recalled record, and a record whose key fails the REL-7 check against the current build's baked_pubkey_ids, which it reads from the pre-run records, so a same-run retract cannot hide it. It is also refused alongside a --make-current for the same pair. The --allow-older help, the OLDER refusal text and RELEASE.md:183 no longer call it a rollback. The new 'Rolling the vendor feed back' section gives commands that parse. The key-rotation forwarding gap is in publish_latest's move_pointer and is recorded under logic-release-6.

verdicts.problems: The ALREADY_FIXED claim holds for the ytdl spelling, which is the only part this chunk owns. The b-roll ingest header at companion/src/ccsync_companion/broll_ingest.py:426-428 is c-broll-music's fix (the X-CCSync-Machine-Pct twin) and is not reviewed here. In companion/src/ccsync_companion/ytdl_executor.py:1097, FleetClient._headers sends _header_safe(_this_machine_id()). That is the minted machine id, not the hostname, and _header_safe (:1020-1039) drops anything that is not printable ASCII. The other two headers are the token and the signed identity token, both ASCII. ytdl/web/ytdlweb/routes_fleet.py:_machine_of reads the body machine_id first, then the query, then the header, so leaving the header out loses nothing. The guard test test_a_non_latin1_machine_id_never_reaches_a_header passes and checks that the body still carries the id. It passes on HEAD by design, which is honest for a guard test.

The fix misses the most common credential refusal. In ytdl_executor.py claim_refusal_sentence (~:1250), the credential branch is `status in (401, 403) and not reason`. But routes_fleet's own identity refusals always carry a reason code: require_identity raises 403 with reason 'identity' when the signed token is expired, invalid, or from a retired key or a deleted user (ytdl/web/ytdlweb/routes_fleet.py:~282-284). It raises 'identity_mismatch' when the report token is bound to another editor (:~176) and 'identity_unconfigured' when the server has no secret (:~266). So the branch only catches require_fleet_token's bare-string 403 and a dashboard-gate 401. An editor whose 30-day identity token has run out presses DOWNLOAD, the claim is refused with reason 'identity', and the page stays silent. That is the exact failure the finding describes. It also contradicts the heartbeat half of this same diff: the heartbeat (:~1293) raises CredentialLost on any 401/403 and hands back 'no longer accepts this computer's sign-in', but the claim for the same verdict says nothing. Only 'identity_unconfigured' is arguably a server problem that should stay quiet. The regression table misses this because it only tests the bare-string 403 (test_bug_hunt_2026_09_24_w2_c-ytdl.py:354) and has no case for reason 'identity' or 'identity_mismatch'. docs/LOOPBACK_API.md's 'a bare credential refusal' matches the code but documents the gap. Fix: treat 403 with reason in {'identity', 'identity_mismatch'} (or any 401/403 whose reason is not attestation, ytdlp_version or identity_unconfigured) as the sign-in sentence, and add parametrised cases. The rest checks out. The reason codes match routes_fleet's claim (attestation, template_version, sidecar_version, out_of_scope with quality, ytdlp_version with min_ytdlp_version, and 409 with claimed_by). The 409 sentence is only said when claimed_by equals the editor, and _already_downloading has no em dash. Ordinary refusals and transport failures stay None. hand_back only sets state, so it adds no blocking IO. progress_row turns the reason into phase 'handed_back', and app.js announceHandBack/watchHandBack reads it. There is no wire change, so version skew is safe both ways. There are no em dashes in the new sentences. The 17 targeted tests pass. A small wording test issue: the 403 {'detail':'no'} case sits in test_an_ordinary_refusal_stays_quiet but asserts handed_back.

(1) The defect is real at HEAD a10ea03. None of SyncEngine, ResolveEngine or LibraryEngine had a stop(). SyncEngine.__getattr__ passes 'stop' to self.res, which has none. So timeline_cards_role._release_engine (companion/src/ccsync_companion/timeline_cards_role.py:861-874) found no callable and did nothing.

(2) The fix covers every long-lived thread a SyncEngine owns:
- The sweep loop: resolve_engine.py _sweep_loop is now `while not self._cards_stopping`.
- The key helper: _let_go runs on the engine's own thread inside run's finally.
- The google-translate worker: translate.py stop() plus the _stopping branch in _worker, which saves _dirty drafts under the lock and returns.
- The media worker: library_engine.py _src_worker drops clip jobs and their marks. Pins stay, because the _pins key is mp_uid, and that is j[0] of the raw queue item. The thread then returns when the queue is dry.
The rest are one-shot threads that end on their own: _transcribe_worker (resolve_engine.py:764), the _tx/_sem/peaks/lite threads, and the keys.py reader, which ends with the helper process.

(3) The stop flag is only checked between ticks, so a running _run_apply or _render_wav always finishes. _serve_held sleeps POLL_FAST and returns, so a HELD engine also exits within a tick.

(4) stop() never blocks the companion: _release_engine calls it with no timeout. A stop before start, and an engine built with object.__new__, are both handled.

(5) The dashboard is unaffected. ProjectAgentEngine.stop (project_agent.py:685) overrides without calling super. ProjectEngine now inherits LibraryEngine.stop, which only stops its translator; its callers are tests that already use `hasattr(engine,'stop')`.

(6) There is no wire change and no version skew.

crash_report.py:294-303 names the second crash in a second '<base>-1.json'. Everything that reads the directory sorts by NAME and treats the last as newest (_crash_files, crash_report.py:176-184, docstring 'Newest LAST'; _prune, 151-153). '-' (0x2d) sorts before '.' (0x2e), so '<base>-1.json' sorts BEFORE '<base>.json'. Probed: two writes in one second gave crash_summary() {'newest': '20260925T100000Z-process.json'}, which is the FIRST crash, and recent_reports ordered them oldest-first. The sync_guard report's 'newest' therefore names the wrong file. _prune also deletes the later crash before the earlier one, and '-10' sorts before '-2'. No crash is lost any more, but the newest-last-by-name invariant this module depends on is broken. Fix: a suffix that sorts after the bare name, e.g. always '<base>-00.json', '<base>-01.json', or '<base>.<nn>.json' with a zero pad, or sort with a key that parses the counter. The dashboard's copy (dashboard crash_report.py:155-164) has the same naming. Check its readers too.

The lane dict and transfers are capped correctly: reporter.py _cap_str/_capped_transfers, applied at ~849-858 and to the top-level current_project at ~888. The caps match api.py, the pass-through of None and "" is kept, and the tests pass. The companion-side fix still misses a field on the same wire. reporter.py:866-871 sends payload["completed"] = list(self._get_completions())[:200] raw. Each entry is built in sync/rclone_lane.py:3898-3902 as {"name": f"{prefix}{name}", ...}, the SAME per-file name as a transfer plus a project-subpath prefix, so it is always at least as long as the transfer name. HEAD's api.CompletedIn declares name max_length=512 (also direction 16, lane 64, at 64) with no before-validator, and the finding names CompletedIn.name explicitly. Consequence: on a dashboard <=0.7.58 (every customer not yet updated), a file whose relative path passes 512 characters has its live transfer truncated by the new code, but its completion record goes out raw on the next report after it finishes, and that whole report 422s. It keeps 422ing until pop_completions has drained, which it does on the attempt even though the report fails, so a single outage lasts one report, but the finding's premise is "never 422 the whole report". The builder capped transfers "because a deep relative path over 512 chars 422s the same way; same wire, same cause" and then did not cap completed, which has the same cause. Fix: run each completed entry through the same capping (name 512, direction 16, lane 64, at 64) in reporter.py before payload["completed"], extend the drift guard test to CompletedIn, and add a regression test with a >512-char completion name.

At HEAD, rclone_lane.py:4531-4535 passes `min_free_bytes=self.disk_floor.min_free_bytes`, so the prune stops at 1x the floor and a parked lane B stays parked, which is the hunter's own failure scenario. fixes.fix: No code change. `--ignore-existing` would do three bad things. (1) It removes the only healing path: after a size mismatch, verify_upload says 'it will be sent again', but the resend would skip the file and exit 0, so the same wrong size would fail on every retry. This can happen when an rclone older than 1.63 writes SFTP uploads in place and leaves a truncated file, or when a verify reads a short size. (2) A foreign file that happens to have the same size would pass the size-only lsjson verify, and the item would go live bound to the wrong audio. That silent mis-binding is worse than an overwrite. (3) It buys nothing for a retry after an upload that already landed, because the resend just rewrites identical bytes. If a guard is ever wanted, it belongs on the server in music-ytdl's mark_uploaded (check size or hash against the recorded transcode), and after this wave nobody needs it. The reasoning is recorded in the Owed round section of the c-broll-music ledger.

Both pages toast any ok:false message other than 'cancelled' (broll/web/static/ingest.js:699-703, music/web/static/ingest.js:508-512), so the wire shape is unchanged and there is no version skew in either direction. The builder called the branch 'dormant', but it is live now: app.py:1666 already registers the lock through set_picker_popup_lock. The regression test only fails on HEAD in the builder's scratch arrangement, because HEAD's popup.py has no PickerBusy. Tests run: 2 of the new picker tests and 6 from test_broll_server.py -k pick, all passed. The unrelated bug-comp-broll-3 hunk at broll_server.py:1177 is also in this file's diff and belongs to a different finding.

None. The NOT_A_DEFECT call covers only the optional companion `--ignore-existing` half, and that is honest. The server-side race is closed in the working tree. music/web/musicweb/routes_ingest.py:396 uses db.claim_dest (db.py:581-618). Under NAME_LOCK it checks disk (NFC and NFD), `tracks` and the unlanded ledger via _name_promised, then creates an O_EXCL placeholder. ingest_batches.py:954 holds the same NAME_LOCK from allocate_name through the commit, so neither ordering lets the two paths share a name. The builder's reasons for declining `--ignore-existing` hold: it would stop a resend from healing a size-mismatched file, and it would turn an overwrite into a silent mis-binding under size-only lsjson verification. One caveat: NAME_LOCK is a threading.Lock, so it is process-wide only. That is fine while the dashboard runs as a single process; it is the music-ytdl group's concern, not this chunk's.

fixes.verified_as: The install script `_INSTALL_KEY_SCRIPT` (printf > tmp; mv -f) replaces authorized_keys. api._install_nas_key_keeping_others calls add_editor_ssh_key when the backend has it, and otherwise merges from find_user()['sshpubkey'], which DSM never fills. So on DSM an approve still replaced the file.
fixes.fix: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/nas/synology.py: new _APPEND_KEY_SCRIPT. It keeps the install script's steps (MISSING_HOME check, umask 077, tmp + mv -f, chown -R of ~/.ssh, chmod 700/600, stat read-back). It copies the old file into the tmp, adds a final newline if the old file lacks one, and appends the key. It writes nothing (ALREADY) when awk finds the same type+body as adjacent fields on any line. New SynologyClient.add_editor_ssh_key refuses a multi-line or one-field key before any SSH, then applies _refuse_non_editor. An account that does not exist goes to create_or_update_editor. A key that was not written (SSH down, MISSING_HOME, non-zero exit) raises NasError through the new _install_ssh_key(append=, unwritten_raises=) arguments, so the approve route keeps the queued offer. StrictModes read-back problems stay warnings. The optional TrueNAS method was not added: api.py already merges against TrueNAS's sshpubkey text. Not live-verified on a DSM box.
